 A fireball seen across southeastern Tennessee last Thursday was a small piece of an asteroid, according to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).
 Residents who had clear skies could see the object speeding towards the earth around 7:45pm. The first sighting was 53 miles above Robbinsville, North Carolina, moving at upwards of 47,000 miles per hour.
 NASA 
 NASA says the chunk of the asteroid was 2 inches in diameter, weighing only 6 ounces.
 It disintegrated at an altitude of 25 miles above East Ridge, just outside Chattanooga.
 All four NASA sky cameras in the region, including the closest to WRCB in Tullahoma, got a good view of it.
 The meteor, NASA says, was not part of the currently active Taurid meteor shower.
